classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange the curve to obtain the squared radius and integrate with respect to y using a logarithmic antiderivative.

content.prompt: The region between the curve $y=\frac{1}{x^2}$ (a truncus) and the $y$-axis from $y=1$ to $y=6$ is rotated about the $y$-axis. Calculate the exact volume of the solid formed.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7 graph below the stem at left
spec.description: Two symmetric branches of the truncus, with arrowheads at all four ends, labelled axes and source numerical ticks. No region, bounds or solution marks are added.
spec.mathematics: y=1/x^2; x is nonzero; horizontal ticks at -3,-2,-1,1,2,3 and vertical ticks at -1,1,2,3,4,5,6.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph remains visible in the question edition.

answer.worked:
$$x^2=\frac{1}{y}$$
$$\begin{align*}
V&=\pi\int_1^6 x^2\,dy\\
V&=\pi\int_1^6\frac{1}{y}\,dy\\
V&=\pi[\ln y]_1^6\\
V&=\pi(\ln 6-\ln 1)\\
V&=\pi\ln 6\text{ units}^3
\end{align*}$$
